ops.title: binrun shim defeats the plugin-root disk override in readAgentsMd (and sibling resolvers)
ops.description:
`readAgentsMd()` (plugins/codex/dispatch.go:248-263) probes two on-disk plugin-root layouts before falling back to its `//go:embed` copy, so a plugin-root `AGENTS.md` is meant to override the embedded developer_instructions feed. Under a real binrun install it never does.

The chain is `bin/codex-ask` (symlink) -> `scripts/install-binary.sh` -> binrun, which `syscall.Exec`s the cached binary directly. Both `os.Executable()` and `selfPath` therefore resolve to `~/.daemonkit/cache/<xx>/<digest>/codex-ask`; `Dir(Dir(exe))` is a cache shard holding only the binary, LICENSE, README, and meta.json. The disk probe misses and the embed always wins.

Verified empirically 2026-07-25: after appending a `## Replies` section to plugins/codex/AGENTS.md, a run invoked as `plugins/codex/bin/codex-ask` recorded a `developer_instructions=` argv element of 1500 chars containing `agent-browser` but NOT `## Replies` — the embedded copy, not the edited disk copy. The printed `AWAIT:` line named the daemonkit cache path, confirming the resolution.

Consequences: the disk-override branch is dead code for every real install (dev symlink installs and the test rigs are its only live callers); no plugin content fed this way can ship without a binary release; and the same trap awaits any future resolver following the pattern — the codex plugin's new `lanes/` and `schemas/` resolvers were deliberately written embed-first because of it.

Proposed fix: export a plugin-root env var (e.g. `CODEX_ASK_PLUGIN_ROOT="$ROOT"`) before each `exec` in the shim and probe it first in the resolver. The shim is generated — edit the shared fragment plugin/guides/sh/binrun-shim.sh (ROOT computed at :27), not the rendered plugins/codex/scripts/install-binary.sh. That fragment is shared with slop-cop, so this wants a fleet-wide look rather than a codex-local patch.

ops.text: A plugin-root AGENTS.md edit changes the developer_instructions recorded in a run's cmd argv on a real binrun install, with no rebuild
The fix lives in plugin/guides/sh/binrun-shim.sh (the shared fragment), not in a rendered install-binary.sh
slop-cop's shim is checked for the same regression before landing
